title: Stochastic batching impact analysis - regional GPU fleet scenarios Q3 2027
summary: Working worksheet to estimate how stochastic (traffic-driven) batching policies interact with quantization profiles across regional GPU fleets. Goal: produce conservative throughput estimates, surface worst-case quality regressions, and recommend operational knobs for SLO adherence under bursty request patterns.
assumptions: Traffic distribution: 60% short-chat (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512)
Baseline hardware: H100 (80GB), A100 (40GB) depending on region; mixed fleet in us-west for cost testing
Quant profiles: FP16 (baseline quality), INT8-PTQ (fast, possible quality delta), INT8-QAT (lower delta), 4-bit hybrid for cold-tier only
Batching policy: adaptive window (max latency 200ms target) with stochastic batching that groups concurrent arrivals; burstiness factor modeled with Poisson lambda variations
KV-cache hit rate: 15% for chat flows (reduces tokens generated), prefix caching applied where available

sensitivity_tests: Vary burst factor from 1.0 -> 3.0 to observe p95 latency and batch size growth
Simulate KV-cache improvements to 30% to measure token cost reduction and effective throughput increase
Test hybrid routing: direct long requests to FP16 pool while short requests served on INT8 pools
Run canary load with 5% traffic on INT8-QAT to validate quality delta on production prompts
key_takeaways: INT8-PTQ can double throughput in steady state but produces measurable quality delta on certain prompt classes (code, instruction-following). Recommend limiting to low-risk workloads or adding A/B evals.
Stochastic batching amplifies p95 latency under bursty traffic (burst factor > 1.8); need latency SLO guardrails (max batch window) to avoid tail latency spikes.
Regional fleet mixes (H100 primary, A100 overflow) give good cost flex but require careful kernel selection to avoid throughput cliffs for long sequences.
4-bit hybrid profiles are attractive for cold-tier cost reduction but have highest quality variance — isolate to background inference where possible.
operational_recommendations: Primary: adopt INT8-QAT for eu-west pilot (36 nodes) with 5% canary traffic and daily quality evaluation against a curated prompt set
Latency control: enforce max batching window of 80ms for chat routes and fall back to single-token streaming when p95 > target
Autoscale: add burst-driven ephemeral capacity (30% headroom) in us-west to smooth stochastic batching impact during peak events
Monitoring: add prompt-set specific quality monitors and link to rollback playbooks for quantized variants
